messages:
Sam H: Heads-up — saw 3 OOMs in prod-eu last night on model x-7b at ~02:10 UTC. Stack traces point to rapid kernel selector toggles + sudden workspace growth.
Priya S: Yep, noticed same. Uploading a heap/profile snapshot: <https://logs.internal/trace/xyz-oom-211345>. KV cache size jumped ~2.3x right before OOM, batching latency also spiked.
Jae K: Hypothesis: allocator fragmentation combined with kernel selector flip when seq_len crosses the long-tail threshold. Selector picks a larger GEMM path (more workspace) briefly, fails allocation, then falls back repeatedly.
Maya_Ops: Can we apply an emergency guard? Suggestion: enable a strict workspace cap and a kernel-stability policy that prefers the smaller predictable kernel under memory pressure. Also throttle per-tenant batch sizes for 30m.
Priya S: On it — I'll push a canary: batching.window_ms -> 50, batching.max_batch_tokens -> 4096, prefer_kernel = "stable_small" for canary pool. Change link: https://config.redwood/c/1234
Sam H: Also add an alert: kernel_switch_rate > 10/min for a node -> page on-call. And OOM_count > 1 in 5m -> auto-enable fallback policy.
Jae K: Implementation notes: we can add a soft KV-cache TTL eviction that triggers when workspace usage > 70% of reserved. Evict by LRU weighted by recent-hit-rate to avoid evicting hot prefixes. Fallback path should spill small KVs to CPU instead of failing.
Maya_Ops: deploy-bot, roll the workspace cap to eu-prod pool (8MB per-worker) and enable kernel-stability toggles for canary nodes.
deploy-bot: rollout started: workspace_cap=8MB -> pool=eu-prod-canary (10%) (initiated by Maya_Ops). CI checks green.
Priya S: Canary config pushed. I'm also patching batching heuristics to prefer eager dispatch for short sequences (<=128) to reduce long-tail buildup. PR: https://gerrit.redwood/4567
Jae K: Preparing allocator tuning PR: reduce initial_bin_size, coalesce_free_runs aggressively, and add transient-buffer-reuse path for KV-ring buffers. This should reduce fragmentation spikes. PR ETA: 6h.
Sam H: Action items: Priya monitor canary for 1hr -> if no regressions, ramp to 50%. Jae prepare prod-safe allocator PR and perf bench. Maya_Ops monitor dashboards and OOM alerts. I'll update the runbook with the new quick toggles and add the kernel_switch_rate panel.
Priya S: Quick test results on staging: OOM repro reduced by 90% with strict workspace cap + prefer_kernel. Latency tail unchanged. Pushing canary now.
Maya_Ops: If OOMs persist after canary, plan B: enable model-variant fallback (x-7b -> x-7b-quant) + per-tenant request shaping (max concurrent requests per API key = 6).
Sam H: Also schedule a nightly perf-regression job that runs candidate kernels against the long-sequence workload to catch selector regressions early.
Priya S: Will add that job. I'll also add telemetry: kernel_choice, workspace_alloc_peak, kv_eviction_events per-request to the trace payload.
Jae K: Noted. I'll include allocator metrics: free-run-count, fragmentation-score, largest-free-chunk in profiler snapshots.
Maya_Ops: Thanks all. Keeping this thread open while canary runs. :thumbsup:
